_about: Graph-value ablation test (B = documents only, C = documents + graph). Six WM-101 cases, each testing something the knowledge graph is meant to guarantee. Every expected fact is traceable to the SOP, work instruction or NCR. 'code' checks are regex (numbers, codes); 'judge' checks are one narrow yes/no question to the Qwen judge, phrased so YES is always the good answer. Locked 2026-09-25.

cases.name: New spool
cases.tests: Finds the defective-spool cause from the 'new spool' clue
cases.incident: WM-101 wire feed motor overload alarm. It started right after we fitted a new wire spool this morning.

checks.q: Does the report identify a defective or newly fitted wire spool as a likely cause?
Does the report recommend replacing the suspect spool with a known-good spool?

checks.label: tension reset to finger-tight + quarter turn

checks.q: Does the report avoid telling the operator to increase drive-roll tension, or to keep adjusting it, as the fix?

cases.name: Tension trap
cases.tests: Warns against the known wrong response and treats repeat alarms as systemic
cases.incident: Third wire feed overload alarm on WM-101 this shift. The operator has been tightening the drive rolls each time.

checks.q: Does the report explicitly warn NOT to keep adjusting or tightening the drive-roll tension?
Does the report say to stop production and inspect the drive rolls and the liner?
Does the report treat three or more overload alarms in one shift as a systemic or recurring equipment fault rather than operator error?
Does the report require lockout/tagout (LOTO) before the repair work?

cases.name: Unstable after liner change
cases.tests: Connects liner replacement to burn-in, a fact in a different document
cases.incident: We just replaced the liner on WM-101 and the wire feed is a bit unstable for the first few minutes. Is something wrong?

checks.q: Does the report say that some wire feed instability in the first minutes after a liner replacement is expected or normal, not a new fault?
Does the report avoid recommending another liner replacement as the immediate fix?

cases.name: Arc voltage
cases.tests: Gives the documented spec and does not use the disputed operator value
cases.incident: WM-101 arc voltage is reading 17 V and the arc is unstable. What should it be?

checks.q: Does the report avoid instructing the operator to set, reset or target an arc voltage of 15-16 V or 15.5 V?
checks.source: SOP 3 overrules the disputed operator note

checks.q: Does the report recommend checking or cleaning the earth clamp?
Does the report say parts welded during the arc instability should be flagged or quarantined for QC inspection?

cases.name: Gas alarm
cases.tests: Critical safety response and what to do with affected parts
cases.incident: Shielding gas pressure low alarm on WM-101 in the middle of a run.

checks.q: Does the report say to stop welding immediately?
Does the report say to check the regulator and the hose connections for leaks?
Does the report say what to do with parts welded after the alarm (scrap them, or hold them for inspection)?
checks.source: SOP 4.4 (scrap) vs gas procedure (hold, SOP Rev 1.1 pending): either accepted

checks.label: criticality rated CRITICAL
checks.source: SOP 4.4: never weld without shielding gas

cases.name: Hot contact tip
cases.tests: Specific numbers and the safe order: cool first, then replace
cases.incident: WM-101 contact tip temperature high alarm. The tip bore looks oval.

checks.q: Does the report say to let the tip cool before touching or replacing it?
Does the report recommend replacing the contact tip?
